subject.title: Add rate limiting and throttling for external API calls

question: What scope should OpenClaw core own for outbound API governance before implementation proceeds?
rationale: The request spans provider dispatch, tools/search, channels/plugins, persistence, cost accounting, CLI/status UX, alerts, and new config contracts; automation cannot safely choose that product/API boundary.

options.title: Provider-Dispatch First
options.body: Accept a narrow opt-in model-provider request pacing layer first, then leave budgets, CLI/status, alerts, and non-provider calls as explicit follow-up decisions.

options.title: Full Core Governance
options.body: Design one broader core policy layer covering providers, tools/search, channel sends, budgets, status, and alerts before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Split Plugin-Owned Pieces
options.body: Keep only missing core/provider API seams in OpenClaw and route channel-specific alerts or optional integrations to plugins or ClawHub.

recommendation.title: Provider-Dispatch First
recommendation.body: Accept a narrow opt-in model-provider request pacing layer first, then leave budgets, CLI/status, alerts, and non-provider calls as explicit follow-up decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the earlier canonical-tracker review and have the strongest product-scoping signal for this cross-cutting provider/config work.
